outcomes.text: Recover the missing counterpart in a comparative clause and decide when a subject is needed.
Select the expression and complement that convey the intended comparison.
Distinguish a ranking in a noun phrase from a free superlative.

key_terms.definition: The clause in a comparison such as than it was or as it is wide, with part of its interpretation supplied by the larger construction.
The group of things or occasions a ranking is made over.
A form such as deepest or most efficiently, used to locate the extreme of a scale within a set.

options.text: The shelf is as deep as it is wide.
options.feedback: The second clause retains wide but leaves its degree unexpressed.

options.text: The shelf is as deep as it is quite wide.
options.feedback: The second clause retains wide but leaves its degree unexpressed.

options.text: The shelf is as deep as it is very wide.
options.feedback: The second clause retains wide but leaves its degree unexpressed.

opening.prompt: Which comparison leaves the degree of width available for as to supply?

options.text: fewer equipment
options.feedback: Equipment has its ordinary mass reading. Fewer ordinarily counts separate items.

options.text: few equipment
options.feedback: Equipment has its ordinary mass reading. Fewer ordinarily counts separate items.

options.text: less equipment
options.feedback: Equipment has its ordinary mass reading. Fewer ordinarily counts separate items.

opening.prompt: Which wording measures an amount of equipment?

options.text: The possible meanings of shelf
options.feedback: The incorporated superlative modifies shelf and ranks it against other shelves.

options.text: The shelves in the case
options.feedback: The incorporated superlative modifies shelf and ranks it against other shelves.

options.text: One shelf across several occasions
options.feedback: The incorporated superlative modifies shelf and ranks it against other shelves.

opening.prompt: What is ranked in “the deepest shelf in the case”?

options.text: Lea works faster than she did last year.
options.feedback: She supplies the subject of did, which stands for the earlier working.

options.text: Lea works faster than did last year.
options.feedback: She supplies the subject of did, which stands for the earlier working.

options.text: Lea works faster than did she last year.
options.feedback: She supplies the subject of did, which stands for the earlier working.

opening.prompt: Which wording keeps a subject for the retained did?

options.text: same screws as last time
options.feedback: This use of same occurs in a definite noun phrase with the.

options.text: some same screws as last time
options.feedback: This use of same occurs in a definite noun phrase with the.

options.text: the same screws as last time
options.feedback: This use of same occurs in a definite noun phrase with the.

opening.prompt: Choose the ordinary phrase naming matching screws.

options.text: Every comparative clause lacks a subject.
options.feedback: The missing position represents the number of brackets ordered.

options.text: The missing subject is the comparative counterpart of more brackets.
options.feedback: The missing position represents the number of brackets ordered.

options.text: Were ordered is the main predicate of more brackets arrived.
options.feedback: The missing position represents the number of brackets ordered.

closing.prompt: Why is the subject absent in “More brackets arrived than were ordered”?

options.text: Rae spoke like she.
options.feedback: As a guide describes the capacity. Like a guide describes resemblance.

options.text: Rae spoke as a guide.
options.feedback: As a guide describes the capacity. Like a guide describes resemblance.

options.text: Rae spoke like a guide.
options.feedback: As a guide describes the capacity. Like a guide describes resemblance.

closing.prompt: Rae really is a guide and spoke in that capacity. Which wording explicitly presents the role?

options.text: The lowest lake is on the left.
options.feedback: Lowest describes the lake’s level. The clause compares it with its level on other occasions.

options.text: The lake is low, which surprises us.
options.feedback: Lowest describes the lake’s level. The clause compares it with its level on other occasions.

options.text: The lake is the lowest it has been all year.
options.feedback: Lowest describes the lake’s level. The clause compares it with its level on other occasions.

closing.prompt: Which sentence has a free superlative with an integrated relative?

options.text: superior to the original / similar to the original
options.feedback: Both adjectives can use to to introduce their standard of comparison.

options.text: superior of the original / similar than the original
options.feedback: Both adjectives can use to to introduce their standard of comparison.

options.text: superior than the original / similar the original
options.feedback: Both adjectives can use to to introduce their standard of comparison.

closing.prompt: Which pair gives ordinary complements in both phrases?

options.text: We used no fasteners other than screws.
options.feedback: Screws is a noun phrase. Those that the store sold is another possible noun phrase.

options.text: We used no fasteners other than the store sold.
options.feedback: Screws is a noun phrase. Those that the store sold is another possible noun phrase.

options.text: We used no fasteners other than were delivered.
options.feedback: Screws is a noun phrase. Those that the store sold is another possible noun phrase.

closing.prompt: Which continuation supplies a noun phrase after postpositive other than?
